name: Seated Quad Sets
name_zh: 坐姿股四头肌等长收缩
description: Sit with leg extended on a flat surface. Tighten the quadriceps by pressing the back of the knee down, hold for 5 seconds, then release.
safety_notes: Stop if sharp pain occurs. Ensure the knee is fully supported.

name: Straight Leg Raises
description: Lie on your back with the uninvolved knee bent. Tighten the quad of the straight leg and lift it to the height of the opposite knee. Hold 3 seconds, lower slowly.
safety_notes: Keep the core engaged. Stop if hip flexor pain occurs.

name: Heel Slides
description: Lie on your back. Slowly slide the heel toward the buttock, bending the knee as far as comfortable, then slide back to starting position.
safety_notes: Move slowly and within pain-free range. Do not force ROM beyond comfort.

name: Prone Knee Flexion
description: Lie face down. Slowly bend the knee bringing the heel toward the buttock. Use a towel loop around the ankle to assist if needed.
safety_notes: Avoid forcing motion. Stop if swelling increases.

name: Standing Hamstring Curls
description: Stand holding a chair for balance. Bend the knee bringing the heel toward the buttock. Hold 2 seconds at the top, then lower slowly.
safety_notes: Keep hips level. Do not compensate with trunk lean.

name: Wall Sits
description: Lean your back flat against a wall and slide down until knees are bent to approximately 45-60 degrees. Hold for 15-30 seconds, then stand back up.
safety_notes: Do not let knees go past 90 degrees. Ensure knees track over toes.

name: Step-Ups
description: Stand in front of a low step (15-20 cm). Step up leading with the involved leg, fully extending the hip and knee. Step down slowly with the uninvolved leg.
safety_notes: Use a handrail if balance is unsteady. Avoid if painful under the kneecap.

name: Mini Squats with Resistance Band
description: Place a resistance band around both thighs just above the knees. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and squat to 45 degrees while pushing knees out against the band.
safety_notes: Do not exceed 60 degrees of knee flexion in early stages. Keep weight on heels.

name: Terminal Knee Extensions
description: Attach a resistance band behind the knee at anchor height. Stand facing the anchor with slight knee bend. Straighten the knee fully against the band resistance.
safety_notes: Focus on the last 30 degrees of extension. Stop if anterior knee pain occurs.

name: Lateral Band Walks
description: Place a resistance band around ankles. Assume a quarter-squat position and step sideways, maintaining tension on the band throughout the movement.
safety_notes: Keep toes pointed forward. Do not let knees collapse inward.

name: Single-Leg Balance on Flat Surface
description: Stand on the involved leg with a slight knee bend. Hold for 30 seconds. Use a wall or chair nearby for safety but try not to touch it.
safety_notes: Ensure safe surroundings. Stop if knee gives way.

name: BOSU Ball Balance
description: Stand on a BOSU ball or unstable surface with the involved leg. Maintain balance for 30 seconds. Progress to eyes closed.
safety_notes: Have a stable object nearby for support. Discontinue if ankle or knee instability is felt.

name: Stationary Bike (Low Resistance)
description: Ride a stationary bike at low resistance. Adjust seat height so knee reaches near-full extension at the bottom of the pedal stroke. Maintain a comfortable cadence.
safety_notes: Start with 10 minutes and progress. Stop if knee swelling increases after session.

name: Knee Flexion Passive ROM Stretch
name_zh: 膝关节屈曲被动关节活动度牵伸
description: Sit on a chair and let gravity assist the knee into flexion. Gently use the opposite foot on top of the involved ankle to add mild overpressure. Hold 30 seconds.
safety_notes: Do not bounce. Pain should be a gentle stretch sensation, not sharp.

name: Prone Hang Knee Extension Stretch
name_zh: 俯卧悬挂膝关节伸展牵伸
description: Lie face down with knees at the edge of a bed so the lower legs hang off. Let gravity gently straighten the knee. Hold for 2 minutes.
safety_notes: Place a small towel roll above the kneecap for comfort. Avoid if posterior knee pain occurs.

name: Standing Calf Raises
description: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a wall for balance. Rise up on toes, hold for 2 seconds, and lower slowly.
safety_notes: Perform bilaterally first, then progress to single leg.

name: IT Band Foam Rolling
description: Lie on your side with the foam roller under the outer thigh. Roll slowly from the hip to just above the knee, pausing on tender spots for 20-30 seconds.
safety_notes: Do not roll directly over the knee joint. Reduce pressure if pain is excessive.

name: Knee Ice Application
description: Apply an ice pack wrapped in a thin towel to the knee. Elevate the leg on a pillow. Keep the ice on for 15-20 minutes.
safety_notes: Never apply ice directly to skin. Remove if numbness occurs. Wait at least 1 hour between applications.

name: Lateral Lunges
description: Stand with feet together. Take a wide step to the side, bending the stepping knee while keeping the other leg straight. Push back to start.
safety_notes: Keep the knee behind the toes. Avoid if medial knee pain occurs.

name: Forward Lunges
description: Stand upright. Step forward with the involved leg, lowering the back knee toward the floor until both knees are near 90 degrees. Push back to standing.
safety_notes: Front knee must not pass the toes. Maintain upright posture.

name: Agility Ladder Drills
description: Perform various foot patterns through an agility ladder including lateral shuffles, in-and-out steps, and single-leg hops. Focus on quick, controlled movements.
safety_notes: Only begin after cleared by PT. Warm up thoroughly. Stop if knee swelling or instability occurs.

name: Box Jumps (Low Height)
description: Stand facing a low box (15-20 cm). Jump onto the box landing softly with both feet, then step down. Focus on soft landing mechanics with knee flexion.
safety_notes: Must be cleared for plyometrics by PT. Land softly with knees tracking over toes.

name: Patellar Mobilization
description: With the knee relaxed and slightly bent, gently glide the kneecap up, down, left, and right using your thumbs and fingers. Hold each direction for 5 seconds.
safety_notes: Use gentle pressure only. Do not perform if significant effusion is present.

name: Single-Leg Deadlift
description: Stand on the involved leg holding a light dumbbell. Hinge at the hip, lowering the weight toward the floor while extending the free leg behind you. Return to standing.
safety_notes: Keep the back flat. Start without weight and progress gradually.

name: Pre-Op Knee Education and Ankle Pumps
name_zh: 术前膝关节教育与踝泵运动
description: Practice ankle pumps by pointing toes up and down rhythmically. Review post-operative exercises and precautions with educational materials.
safety_notes: This is a preparatory exercise. Ensure understanding of post-op restrictions.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
description: Stand near a wall for support. Bend the knee and grasp the ankle, pulling the heel toward the buttock. Hold for 30 seconds.
safety_notes: Keep knees together. Avoid arching the lower back.

name: Hamstring Stretch (Supine)
description: Lie on your back. Lift one leg and hold behind the thigh. Gently straighten the knee until a stretch is felt in the back of the thigh. Hold for 30 seconds.
safety_notes: Keep the opposite leg flat on the ground. Do not bounce.

name: Tandem Walking
description: Walk in a straight line placing the heel of one foot directly in front of the toes of the other foot. Take 10-15 steps, turn, and repeat.
safety_notes: Perform near a wall for safety. Look forward, not at feet.

name: Retro Walking (Backward Walking)
description: Walk backward slowly in a clear, safe space. Focus on controlled knee extension as each foot contacts the ground behind you.
safety_notes: Ensure the path is clear. Have a spotter or wall nearby.

name: Quad Foam Rolling
description: Lie face down with the foam roller under the front of the thigh. Roll from hip to just above the kneecap, pausing on tender areas for 20-30 seconds.
safety_notes: Avoid rolling directly on the knee. Reduce pressure as needed.

name: Swimming (Freestyle / Kicking)
description: Swim freestyle or perform flutter kicking with a kickboard in a pool. The buoyancy reduces joint stress while building cardiovascular fitness and leg strength.
safety_notes: Avoid breaststroke kick if medial knee pain exists. Ensure the surgical wound is fully healed.

name: Pendulum Exercises (Codman's)
description: Lean forward at the waist, letting the involved arm hang freely. Gently swing the arm in small circles (clockwise and counterclockwise), then forward-back and side-to-side.
safety_notes: Use body momentum, not arm muscles. Keep movements small and pain-free.

name: Passive Shoulder Flexion (Supine)
description: Lie on your back. Use the uninvolved hand to lift the involved arm overhead as far as comfortable. Hold at end range for 5 seconds, then lower.
safety_notes: Stay within pain-free range. Do not actively lift with the involved arm in early stages.

name: Table Slides (Shoulder Flexion)
description: Sit at a table with a towel under the hand. Slide the arm forward along the table, assisting shoulder flexion. Slide back to start.
safety_notes: Keep the shoulder relaxed. Let the table support the arm's weight.

name: Shoulder Isometric External Rotation
description: Stand with the elbow bent at 90° and the back of the hand against a wall or door frame. Push outward into the wall with 50% effort, hold for 5 seconds.
safety_notes: No pain should be felt. Keep elbow at the side.

name: Shoulder Isometric Internal Rotation
description: Stand in a doorway with the elbow at 90°. Press the palm into the door frame with 50% effort, hold for 5 seconds, release.
safety_notes: Avoid shrugging the shoulder. Maintain submaximal effort.

name: External Rotation with Resistance Band
description: Anchor a resistance band at elbow height. Stand sideways, elbow at 90° and tucked to the side. Rotate the forearm outward against the band, then return slowly.
safety_notes: Use a light band initially. Stop if pain occurs in the rotator cuff region.

name: Internal Rotation with Resistance Band
description: Anchor a resistance band at elbow height. Stand sideways, elbow at 90° and tucked to the side. Rotate the forearm inward against the band, then return slowly.
safety_notes: Use light resistance. Keep the elbow pinned to the side throughout.

name: Scapular Retraction (Squeeze)
description: Sit or stand with arms at the sides. Squeeze the shoulder blades together and down, hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
safety_notes: Do not shrug shoulders up. Focus on pulling blades toward the spine.

name: Scapular Wall Push-Ups
description: Stand facing a wall, hands at shoulder height and width. Lean toward the wall bending elbows, then push back. At end range, push further to protract scapulae.
safety_notes: Keep elbows close to the body. Do not elevate shoulders.

name: Supine Shoulder Abduction Passive ROM
description: Lie on your back. Use the opposite hand or a wand to move the involved arm out to the side (abduction), keeping the elbow straight. Hold at end range for 5 seconds.
safety_notes: Stay within 90° of abduction in early rehab. Progress gradually.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
description: Bring the involved arm across the chest. Use the opposite hand to gently pull the arm closer to the body. Hold for 30 seconds.
safety_notes: Do not force the stretch. Avoid if posterior shoulder pain is acute.

name: Sleeper Stretch
description: Lie on the involved side with the shoulder and elbow at 90°. Use the opposite hand to gently push the forearm toward the floor (internal rotation). Hold for 30 seconds.
safety_notes: Be very gentle. Stop if sharp pain occurs. Not recommended in early post-op phase.

name: Shoulder Flexion with Light Dumbbell
description: Stand holding a light dumbbell (1-2 kg). Raise the arm forward to shoulder height (90° flexion) with the thumb pointing up. Hold 2 seconds, lower slowly.
safety_notes: Start with very light weight. Do not go above shoulder height until cleared by PT.

name: Shoulder Abduction with Light Dumbbell
description: Stand holding a light dumbbell. Raise the arm out to the side to shoulder height in the scapular plane (30° forward). Hold 2 seconds, lower slowly.
safety_notes: Lead with the elbow slightly. Avoid shrugging the shoulder.

name: Prone Y-T-W Raises
description: Lie face down on a mat. Raise arms into Y position (overhead), T position (out to sides), and W position (elbows bent, retracted). Hold each for 3 seconds.
safety_notes: Start without weights. Progress to light dumbbells only when form is perfect.

name: Shoulder External Rotation at 90° Abduction
description: Stand with the arm abducted to 90° and elbow bent at 90°. Using a resistance band, rotate the forearm upward (external rotation). Return slowly.
safety_notes: Must have full pain-free ROM before adding resistance. Stop if impingement symptoms appear.

name: Doorway Pec Stretch
description: Stand in a doorway with elbows at 90° and forearms on the frame. Step forward gently until a stretch is felt across the chest. Hold for 30 seconds.
safety_notes: Keep elbows at or below shoulder level. Do not overstretch.

name: Shoulder Shrugs
description: Stand with arms at the sides. Shrug both shoulders up toward the ears, hold for 3 seconds, then relax. Progress to light dumbbells.
safety_notes: This targets the upper trapezius. Avoid if it increases neck tension.

name: Shoulder Pulley Exercises
description: Sit under a door pulley system. Use the uninvolved arm to pull the rope down, lifting the involved arm up into flexion. Control the motion in both directions.
safety_notes: Movement should be slow and controlled. The involved arm remains passive.

name: Shoulder Ice Application
description: Apply an ice pack wrapped in a towel over the shoulder joint. Rest in a supported position for 15-20 minutes.
safety_notes: Never apply ice directly to skin. Remove if excessive numbness occurs.

name: Arm Ergometer (Upper Body Bike)
description: Use an upper body ergometer at low resistance. Pedal forward for 7 minutes, then backward for 7 minutes. Maintain comfortable speed.
safety_notes: Adjust the height so shoulders are not elevated. Stop if impingement pain occurs.

name: Resisted Rows with Band
description: Anchor a resistance band at waist height. Stand facing the anchor and pull the band toward the waist, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Return slowly.
safety_notes: Keep elbows close to the body. Do not arch the back.

name: Sidelying External Rotation
description: Lie on the uninvolved side with the involved elbow at 90° resting on a towel roll at the waist. Rotate the forearm upward, hold 2 seconds, lower slowly.
safety_notes: Start with no weight or very light (0.5 kg). Keep elbow on the towel roll throughout.

name: Shoulder Pre-Op Education and Grip Strengthening
name_zh: 术前肩关节教育与握力训练
description: Practice hand/wrist/grip exercises with a stress ball or towel squeeze. Review post-surgical sling use and precautions. Practice one-handed daily tasks.
safety_notes: Avoid any forceful shoulder movements pre-operatively if instructed.

name: Overhead Shoulder Press (Light)
description: Stand holding light dumbbells at shoulder height. Press overhead until arms are fully extended, then lower slowly to shoulder height.
safety_notes: Only perform when cleared for overhead activities by PT. Keep core engaged.

name: Upper Trap Stretch
description: Sit in a chair. Tilt the head to one side bringing the ear toward the shoulder. Gently apply pressure with the same-side hand. Hold for 30 seconds per side.
safety_notes: Do not force the stretch. Keep the opposite shoulder down.

name: Chest Press with Resistance Band
description: Anchor a band behind you at chest height. Hold ends in each hand and press forward, extending the arms. Return slowly.
safety_notes: Keep shoulder blades stable. Avoid if anterior shoulder pain occurs.

name: Plank (Modified on Knees)
description: Assume a plank position on knees and forearms. Maintain a straight line from head to knees. Hold for 15-30 seconds.
safety_notes: Do not allow the hips to sag. Stop if shoulder pain occurs.

name: Prone Shoulder Extension
description: Lie face down with arms at the sides, palms facing the ceiling. Lift both arms toward the ceiling, squeezing shoulder blades together. Hold 3 seconds, lower.
safety_notes: Keep the neck neutral. Do not hyperextend the lower back.

name: Wand-Assisted Shoulder ER Stretch
description: Hold a stick with both hands, elbows at 90° by your sides. Use the uninvolved hand to push the stick, rotating the involved shoulder externally. Hold at end range for 5 seconds.
safety_notes: Do not force rotation. Keep the elbow pinned at the waist.

name: Ball Squeezes (Isometric Adduction)
description: Hold a small exercise ball or pillow between the elbow and the side of the body. Squeeze and hold for 5 seconds, then release.
safety_notes: Use gentle to moderate pressure. This exercise is safe in early rehab.

name: Walk with Arm Swing Coordination
name_zh: 步行配合手臂摆动协调训练
description: Walk at a comfortable pace, gradually incorporating natural arm swing with the involved arm. Start with small swings and increase amplitude over time.
safety_notes: Use sling if still in immobilization phase. Only swing as tolerated.

name: Shoulder Blade Clocks
description: Stand facing a wall with the hand on an exercise ball at shoulder height. Move the ball in small clockwise and counterclockwise circles, focusing on scapular control.
safety_notes: Keep the arm below shoulder height if overhead is restricted. Maintain gentle pressure on the ball.

name: Cat-Cow Stretch
description: On hands and knees, alternate between arching the back (cow) and rounding the back (cat). Move slowly, coordinating with breathing.
safety_notes: Keep movements within a pain-free range. Avoid if acute disc herniation symptoms are present.

name: Pelvic Tilts (Supine)
description: Lie on your back with knees bent. Flatten the lower back into the floor by tightening the abdominals and tilting the pelvis. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
safety_notes: This is a gentle exercise. Ensure you are activating the deep core, not holding breath.

name: Bridges (Glute Bridge)
description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat. Squeeze the glutes and lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. Hold 5 seconds, lower.
safety_notes: Do not hyperextend the lower back at the top. Keep core engaged.

name: Bird-Dog Exercise
description: On hands and knees, simultaneously extend the right arm forward and the left leg backward. Hold for 5 seconds. Return and switch sides.
safety_notes: Keep the spine neutral—do not rotate the hips or arch the back.

name: Dead Bug Exercise
description: Lie on your back with arms reaching toward the ceiling and knees bent at 90°. Slowly lower the right arm and left leg toward the floor, then return. Alternate sides.
safety_notes: Keep the lower back flat on the floor throughout. Exhale during the extension phase.

name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
description: Lie on your back. Pull one knee toward the chest with both hands. Hold for 20-30 seconds. Repeat on the other side, then both knees.
safety_notes: Do not bounce. Avoid if flexion-intolerant back pain is present.

name: Prone Press-Up (McKenzie Extension)
description: Lie face down. Place hands under the shoulders and press up, extending the spine while keeping the hips on the floor. Hold for 3 seconds, lower.
safety_notes: This is an extension exercise. Avoid if extension worsens symptoms. Do not force range.

name: Child's Pose
description: Kneel on the floor and sit back on the heels. Reach arms forward along the floor, lowering the chest toward the thighs. Hold for 30 seconds, breathing deeply.
safety_notes: Place a pillow under the stomach if needed. Avoid if deep flexion causes pain.

name: Side Plank (Modified)
description: Lie on your side with the elbow under the shoulder and knees bent. Lift the hips off the ground, forming a straight line from head to knees. Hold for 15-20 seconds per side.
safety_notes: Avoid if it triggers lateral back or hip pain. Keep the body in a straight line.

name: Supine Spinal Twist
description: Lie on your back with knees bent. Let both knees fall gently to one side while keeping the shoulders flat. Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
safety_notes: Move within a comfortable range. Avoid if rotational movements exacerbate symptoms.

name: Plank Hold (Forearm)
description: Assume a forearm plank position. Maintain a straight line from head to heels. Engage the core and hold for 20-30 seconds.
safety_notes: Do not let hips sag or pike up. Breathe normally throughout.

name: Clamshells
description: Lie on your side with knees bent at 45°. Keeping feet together, open the top knee like a clamshell. Hold 2 seconds at the top, close slowly. Add a band for resistance.
safety_notes: Do not roll the pelvis backward. Keep the core engaged.

name: Walking Program (Level Surface)
description: Walk on a flat surface at a comfortable pace. Start with 10-15 minutes and progress to 30 minutes. Focus on upright posture and natural arm swing.
safety_notes: Wear supportive shoes. Stop if pain increases significantly.

name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneeling)
description: Kneel on one knee with the opposite foot in front. Shift weight forward while keeping the trunk upright until a stretch is felt in the front of the hip. Hold for 30 seconds.
safety_notes: Do not arch the lower back. Squeeze the glute of the kneeling side.

name: Piriformis Stretch (Figure-4)
description: Lie on your back. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Pull the uncrossed thigh toward the chest until a stretch is felt in the buttock. Hold for 30 seconds per side.
safety_notes: Keep the head and shoulders relaxed on the floor. Do not force the stretch.

name: Seated Lumbar Rotation
description: Sit in a chair with feet flat. Cross arms over the chest. Slowly rotate the trunk to one side, hold for 5 seconds, then rotate to the other side.
safety_notes: Move slowly and within a comfortable range. Avoid if rotation worsens radiating symptoms.

name: Stability Ball Seated Marching
description: Sit on a stability ball with feet flat. Alternately lift each foot off the floor in a marching motion while maintaining balance and an upright posture.
safety_notes: Start near a wall for support. Ensure the ball is properly sized.

name: Stability Ball Back Extension
description: Lie face down draped over a stability ball with toes on the floor. Place hands behind the head and extend the spine upward. Hold 3 seconds, lower.
safety_notes: Do not hyperextend. Keep the movement controlled.

name: Aquatic Walking
description: Walk in waist-deep water at a comfortable pace. The buoyancy reduces spinal loading while providing gentle resistance for strengthening.
safety_notes: Use a pool with safe footing. Do not walk in water deeper than chest level without supervision.

name: Lower Back Ice/Heat Application
description: Apply an ice pack (for acute flare-ups) or heat pack (for chronic stiffness) to the lower back for 15-20 minutes. Lie in a comfortable position.
safety_notes: Wrap in a towel. Alternate ice and heat if appropriate. Do not fall asleep on a heat pack.

name: Superman Exercise
description: Lie face down with arms extended overhead. Simultaneously lift arms, chest, and legs off the floor. Hold for 3-5 seconds, lower.
safety_notes: Keep neck in a neutral position. Do not jerk into the position—lift smoothly.

name: Single-Leg Bridge
description: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg extended straight. Lift the hips off the floor using the bent leg. Hold 3 seconds, lower.
safety_notes: Keep the pelvis level—do not let it drop on the unsupported side.

name: Standing Hip Abduction
description: Stand with a resistance band around the ankles. Lift one leg out to the side against the band resistance. Hold 2 seconds, return slowly. Repeat on both sides.
safety_notes: Keep the trunk upright—do not lean to the side. Hold a chair for balance if needed.

name: Pallof Press (Anti-Rotation)
description: Anchor a band at chest height. Stand sideways to the anchor, holding the band at the chest. Press the band straight out, resisting the rotational pull. Hold for 3 seconds, return.
safety_notes: Engage the core throughout. Do not let the trunk rotate toward the anchor.

name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
description: Sit on the edge of a chair. Extend one leg with the heel on the floor. Hinge forward at the hips keeping the back straight until a stretch is felt. Hold for 30 seconds.
safety_notes: Do not round the back. Hinge from the hips.

name: Standing Balance with Eyes Closed
description: Stand on both feet with eyes closed for 30 seconds. Progress to single-leg stance. Focus on maintaining upright posture using proprioception.
safety_notes: Perform near a wall or stable surface for safety. Have a spotter if needed.

name: Elliptical Trainer (Low Impact)
description: Use an elliptical trainer at low resistance. Maintain an upright posture and engage the core. Start with 10-15 minutes and progress.
safety_notes: Avoid leaning forward excessively. Stop if back pain increases.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
description: Lie on your back with one hand on the chest and one on the abdomen. Breathe in slowly through the nose, feeling the abdomen rise. Exhale slowly through pursed lips.
safety_notes: Keep the chest relatively still. Focus on expanding the lower ribs and abdomen.

name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
description: Lie comfortably. Systematically tense each muscle group for 5 seconds, then relax for 15 seconds. Start from the feet and progress to the head.
safety_notes: Do not tense muscles around a surgical site. Skip any areas that are painful.

name: Gentle Full-Body Stretching Routine
description: Perform a head-to-toe gentle stretching routine: neck rolls, shoulder circles, trunk rotations, hamstring stretch, quad stretch, and calf stretch. Hold each 20 seconds.
safety_notes: Avoid stretching directly through surgical areas in early rehab. Breathe normally.

name: Tai Chi Basic Movements
description: Perform basic Tai Chi movements: weight shifting, single-leg stance transitions, and slow arm movements. Focus on slow, controlled, flowing movements with deep breathing.
safety_notes: Avoid deep stances if knee or back pain is present. Move within comfortable range.

name: Yoga: Warrior II Pose (Modified)
description: Stand with feet wide apart. Turn one foot out 90° and bend that knee to approximately 90°. Extend arms to the sides at shoulder height. Hold for 20-30 seconds per side.
safety_notes: Keep the bent knee behind the toes. Modify depth as needed.

name: Recumbent Bike Cardio
description: Ride a recumbent bike at moderate resistance. The reclined position reduces stress on the back and knees. Maintain a comfortable cadence for 15-20 minutes.
safety_notes: Adjust the seat to allow near-full knee extension. Start with low resistance.

name: Resistance Band Chest Fly
description: Anchor a band behind you at chest height. Hold the ends and bring the hands together in front of the chest in a hugging motion. Return slowly.
safety_notes: Keep a slight bend in the elbows. Avoid if anterior shoulder pain is present.

name: Guided Meditation for Pain Management
description: Find a comfortable position. Close your eyes and focus on slow, deep breathing. Use visualization to imagine warmth and healing in the affected area. Practice for 10-15 minutes.
safety_notes: This is a mental health exercise. There are no physical contraindications.

name: Yoga: Tree Pose (Modified)
description: Stand on one leg. Place the sole of the opposite foot on the inner calf (not the knee). Bring hands to prayer position at the chest. Hold for 20-30 seconds per side.
safety_notes: Never place the foot against the knee joint. Stand near a wall for safety. Modify by keeping toes on the floor.
